title: Brain-Hand protocol v1
description: Wire contract between the brain (LLM harness) and a hand (tool executor in a microVM). One multiplexed WebSocket per hand carries JSON text frames: the brain sends `Request` frames, the hand sends `HandFrame` frames (responses correlated by `id`, plus unsolicited `hand_status` events). Major version must match; unknown fields are ignored. Semantics live in contracts/abi/v1/README.md.

RequestId.description: Brain-minted, unique per request on one connection. Responses echo it.

OperationId.description: Brain-minted, durable, unique per tool-call attempt. Not the provider's tool_call id.

LaneId.description: Brain-minted lane identifier. "0" is the root lane and always exists.

BatchId.description: Groups the parallel tool calls of one assistant message.

GenerationId.description: Minted by the hand per incarnation (per boot with fresh state). Lanes, operations and spill files are scoped to a generation.

BootId.description: Changes on every VM boot, including resume from a released state. Same generation_id + same boot_id on reconnect means in-guest state survived.

ManifestId.description: Identifies one workspace sync manifest. Brain-minted.

PackId.description: Identifies one sync pack object (tar+zstd of changed files). Brain-minted.

MonotonicMs.description: Milliseconds on the guest's monotonic clock. Jumps across a restore; compare only within one boot_id.

WallMs.description: Milliseconds since the Unix epoch, guest wall clock.

major.description: Must match exactly between brain and hand.

Stream.description: Every operation owns two byte streams. Typed tools write their human-readable result to stdout and diagnostics to stderr.

offset.description: Byte offset into the full stream as produced (not as retained).
Byte offset of the first byte of `data_base64` in the full stream.

data_base64.description: Standard base64 (RFC 4648 §4, with padding). Bounded by `max_bytes` of the request and `limits.max_slice_bytes`.

eof.description: True when this slice reaches the current end of the stream. Only meaningful as 'no more bytes right now'; the stream may still grow while the operation is running.

produced_bytes.description: Total bytes the child has written to this stream so far.

retained_from.description: Bytes before this offset are evicted (bounds.max_retained_bytes). A poll below this offset returns `operation_output_evicted`; absent is not zero.

spill_path.description: Guest path of the file holding the retained bytes, readable by the agent's own tools (e.g. `grep`). Deleted on `release`.

sha256.description: Over the full stream. Present only once the operation is terminal and nothing was evicted.

Bounds.description: Per-operation limits enforced by the hand. Missing fields take `limits.default_bounds`.

timeout_ms.description: Relative deadline on the guest monotonic clock. null = no hand-side timeout.

max_retained_bytes.description: Per stream. Beyond this the oldest bytes are evicted from the spill file (tail retention).

EffectiveBounds.description: The complete bounds a hand applies when `start.bounds` omits a field.

parent.description: Required when mode = ephemeral: the lane whose environment is inherited. An ephemeral lane's env mutations are discarded when it is closed or its operation ends.

inflight.description: The attached operation currently holding the lane, if any.

required_env.description: Environment-key names in the execution seal; values arrive separately in hello.env.

get_url.description: Required for a staged bundle; absent for a checksum-known preinstalled executable.

streams.description: Hint for the brain: whether stdout is UTF-8 text. Default text.

ToolManifest.description: The exact ordered sealed Hand tool set. Digest = SHA-256 over RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON. Array order is significant.

Limits.description: Declared by the hand in `hello`, not assumed by the brain.

max_frame_bytes.description: Largest WebSocket text frame either side will send.

max_slice_bytes.description: Largest decoded slice returned per stream per response.

spill_dir.description: Where operation output files live. Not synced.

Usage.description: Observation only; customer-controlled data; never billing authority (I9).

Outcome.description: completed = the tool ran to its end (a non-zero exit_code is still `completed`; the failure is data for the model). failed = the hand could not run it. interrupted = outcome unknown; never replayed.

exit_code.description: Process exit code for command-like tools; null when killed by a signal. Typed tools use 0 = ok, 1 = tool-level failure explained on stderr.

output.description: Typed result validated against the tool's `output_schema`. Present when outcome = completed.

OperationStatus.description: missing = the hand knows the id but lost its record (treated as interrupted).

retryable.description: True only when repeating the identical request later is safe and may succeed (e.g. resource_exhausted). Never true for opaque work.

details.description: Code-specific structured detail, e.g. {"schema_path": ...} for tool_input_invalid.

roots.description: Absolute directories included in workspace sync (default: workspace and home).

exclude.description: Gitignore-style patterns relative to each root.

RestoreSource.description: How a fresh hand re-materialises the workspace. All URLs are short-lived presigned GETs minted by the trusted side; the hand holds no credential (I8).

HelloRequest.description: First request on every connection. Seals the tool manifest (I1), authenticates the brain to the hand, restores the workspace on a fresh generation, re-attaches on reconnect.

session_token.description: Per-session secret the hand was launched with. Mismatch = unauthorized and the connection is closed.

expected_generation_id.description: Set on reconnect. If the hand's generation differs, the response still succeeds and the brain treats every prior operation as lost.

tool_manifest_digest.description: The execution-seal digest selected at session create.

tool_manifest.description: The exact manifest to stage and acknowledge. Bundle URLs are short-lived and excluded from model-visible definitions.

env.description: Environment for lane 0 (inherited by every lane). Customer-supplied; never platform credentials.

restore.description: Present when the hand is a fresh generation of a session that has synced before. The hand restores before answering.

tools.description: The manifest's tools in the exact sealed order.

lanes.description: Every lane the hand knows (live and closed tombstones). Non-empty only on reconnect to a surviving generation.

operations.description: Every non-released operation. Empty on a fresh generation.

StartRequest.description: Begin a tool call. Idempotent within a generation by (operation_id, call_hash): a replay returns the existing operation without running it again. Validation precedes side effects.

call_hash.description: SHA-256 over JCS of {tool, input, lane, cwd, detach, bounds}. Same operation_id with a different call_hash = operation_idempotency_conflict.

input.description: Validated against the manifest input_schema before anything runs.

cwd.description: Working directory for this call. Default = paths.workspace. Per call; the lane's cwd is never mutated by the ABI.

detach.description: true = background job: return as soon as the operation is recorded and spawned; the lane is not held; poll/cancel later. false = attached: holds the lane until terminal.

wait_ms.description: Attached only: wait up to this long for the operation to become terminal before answering, so short calls cost one round trip. Capped by limits.max_poll_wait_ms. Ignored when detach = true.

max_bytes.description: Bytes of stdout/stderr (from offset 0) to include in the response slices. 0 = none.

correlation.description: Opaque to the hand (e.g. agent_id, provider tool_call id). Echoed on every view.

replayed.description: True when this start matched an existing (operation_id, call_hash) and nothing new was executed.

PollRequest.description: Status plus incremental output from byte cursors. Byte offsets are the authority: no gaps, no duplicates, up to retention. Waits up to wait_ms for the operation to become terminal or for any cursor to have new bytes.

max_bytes.description: Total decoded bytes across all returned slices.

CancelRequest.description: SIGTERM to the operation's process group -> grace_ms -> SIGKILL -> terminal(cancelled). Cancelling a terminal operation is not an error (accepted = false).

view.description: The view at the time of the answer; may still be running during the grace period.

ReleaseRequest.description: The brain has durably committed these results; the hand deletes their spill files and forgets them. After release, poll returns operation_not_found and a replayed start would run again — so release only after commit.

unknown.description: Ids the hand did not know (already released or never started). Not an error.

LaneCloseRequest.description: Destroy a lane and tombstone its id. Cancels its attached in-flight operation. Does not kill detached jobs started from it (they belong to the operation registry). Lane 0 is not closable.

get_url.description: Short-lived presigned GET minted by the trusted side.

sha256.description: Verified after download; mismatch = checksum_mismatch and the file is not written.

path.description: Absolute guest path inside the sync scope; parents are created. Symlinks are resolved before the scope check.

PutRequest.description: Files in. Bytes never travel as a tool result (I7): the hand downloads from presigned URLs, or accepts small inline payloads.

path.description: Absolute guest path inside the sync scope, resolved through symlinks.

name.description: Session-unique artifact name, chosen by the brain/customer.

put_url.description: Short-lived presigned PUT for exactly this artifact object.

media_type.description: Sent as Content-Type. Sniffed if absent.

PersistRequest.description: Files out. The hand uploads each item to its presigned URL and reports size + digest; the trusted side records the artifact. Bounded by limits.max_persist_bytes per item.

SyncRequest.description: Workspace sync: diff the sync scope against the last manifest, upload changed files as one pack plus a new manifest. Brain-driven (turn end, every sync_interval, before release/termination). Nothing is uploaded when nothing changed.

manifest_id.description: Id for the manifest this sync would produce.

full.description: true = pack every file (compaction), not only changed ones. The new manifest then references a single pack.

changed.description: false = nothing differed from the last manifest; no upload happened and manifest_id is the previous one.

packs_referenced.description: How many packs the new manifest points at. The brain compacts (full = true) when this grows large.

RequestCall.description: One brain->hand call, tagged by `op`; `args` is that op's request type.

Request.description: Brain -> hand. Every request carries the brain's ownership fence; a fence lower than the highest the hand has accepted is refused with fence_stale (no side effect). generation_id is required on every request except hello; a mismatch is generation_mismatch.

Response.description: Hand -> brain answer to one Request, correlated by `id`.

psi_some_avg10.description: PSI memory 'some' avg10, when the guest kernel exposes it.

HandStatusEvent.description: Hand -> brain, unsolicited: on every idle/busy transition, when a detached job ends, and every heartbeat_ms. The idle signal.

idle_for_ms.description: 0 while inflight or live_jobs is non-empty.

pack_id.description: The pack whose entry `path` holds this exact content.

SyncManifest.description: The object a sync writes to manifest_put_url. Restore = fetch this, then the referenced packs, then extract each file entry from its pack. Empty directories and symlinks are recreated from entries.

pack_format.description: POSIX pax tar, zstd-compressed; entry names are absolute guest paths without the leading slash.

Reply.description: One successful reply, tagged by `op`; `body` is that op's response type.
